To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Mt Halimun Salak Malaise Trap Project is the largest DNA Barcode library ever published from the Indonesian Archipelago, that the library is highly species-rich and that the library includes many species that are likely to be new to science.
1) the DNA barcode library of the Mount Halimum-Salak area is the most species rich for Indonesia and 2) that this library contains a large number of species new to science.
the Mt Halimun Salak Malaise trap project is releasing the most species-rich DNA Barcode library for the Indonesian entomological community.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery and description of new species, and with the establishment of a reference library for DNA barcoding of insects in West Java.
the inventorying of the biodiversity in a tropical forest in West Java.
the inventorying of the Indonesian entomo fauna using molecular methods, with a focus in the Mount Halimum-Salak area, West Java.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Halimun Salak National Park harbours one of the most diverse entomofaunas in Indonesia and that the biodiversity inventory of the area has just started.

our study provides the first large scale DNA barcoding effort in Indonesia, which shows that DNA barcoding is a powerful tool for biodiversity assessment and inventory in tropical areas, especially when combined with Malaise traps.
the Indonesian entomological inventory is far from complete and there is a pressing need for further exploration and taxonomic work, especially in the most species rich groups of insects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Mt Halimun Salak National Park is a biodiversity hotspot for insects, but that we are only scratching the surface of the diversity present in the area.

the DNA barcoding of the Halimum-Salak National park yielded 1,195 putative species, of which 804 were singletons, and 1,149 were new to Biodiversity Heritage Library, and that the cost/benefits relationship of the discovery new species in the areas sampled is very high.

we were successful in generating the largest DNA barcode library for Indonesia, which is also the most species rich barcode library for the Hymenopteran, Coleopteran, Dipteran and Lepidopteran fauna of the country.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the DNA barcoding pipeline is a powerful tool to rapidly increase the knowledge of the biodiversity in tropical areas, especially in areas that have not been studied before, or where taxonomic knowledge is scarce or non-existing.
, with a small number of specimens, we were able to discover a large proportion of BINs, which is indicative of the high biodiversity of the area.

the Indonesian entomological community needs to be aware of the possibilities of DNA barcoding and the BOLD system, and that it needs to embrace the use of these technologies in order to achieve the goal of a taxonomically sound inventory.
